title: Attention kernel microtiling, mixed-precision fallback, and prefill/decode pacing
text:
Attention kernel microtiling, mixed-precision fallback, and prefill/decode pacing

description:
Problem: We integrated FlashAttention v3 kernels into the runtime selector but are seeing intermittent latency tail regressions and memory pressure on long-prefill workloads. Some customers report p99 spikes on 4-8k token prefill jobs and occasional OOMs during bursts.

Goal: Harden the kernel selection path with microtiling heuristics and a safe mixed-precision fallback so v3 can be used where it helps throughput without regressing latency or reliability. Implement prefill/decode pacing heuristics to reduce peak memory and avoid cluster-wide backpressure.

Scope:
- Add microtiling tensor-slice scoring to the kernel selector (prefer smaller tiles on high-seq small-batch workloads)
- Add a mixed-precision compatibility check and a fast fallback to v2-like kernel when memory or numerical stability risk is high
- Implement a two-pass prefill option (chunked-prefill) that lowers peak KV cache allocation for long contexts
- Add decode pacing that reserves GPU slots for low-latency streams to avoid batch-filling degeneracy

Acceptance criteria:
- No p99 regression vs runtime-1.18 on our long-prefill benchmark suite (8k and 16k tokens) across at least A100 and H100 instance types
- Peak memory reduced by >=15% for problematic workloads in our stress tests
- Reproducible experiment demonstrating fallback correctness and negligible throughput loss for common batches

comments:
2026-03-02 - Ticket created by Marina: initial report consolidated from SRE and two enterprise customers. Linked traces and stack dumps. Priority set to P1 due to customer-visible p99 spikes.
2026-03-03 - Devon: Reproduced p99 spike locally. Workload: batch size 2, seq=8k prefill then decode. FlashAttention v3 improved mean throughput but p99 increased by ~18% compared to v2. Observed peak GPU memory +24% on A100-80GB.
2026-03-05 - Devon: Profiling notes: v3 microkernel packs tiles for improved warp utilization but produces transient allocation patterns that amplify KV cache resident memory. Identified two hotspots in kernel chooser: (1) tiling score ignores batch skew, (2) no numeric-stability check for bfloat16 path on some attention dims.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4987 - add microtiling scorer and batch-skew penalty. Preliminary bench shows p99 down 6% on seq=8k for batch=2, mean throughput unchanged. Requesting eng review.
2026-03-09 - Experiment: chunked-prefill prototype (split 8k into 2x4k prefill passes) reduced peak mem by ~18% but increased total prefill time by ~9%; decode tail improved due to fewer OOMs and less GC. Trade-off: higher end-to-end latency for cold-start single-request flows; benefits burst scenarios.
2026-03-10 - Alex (SRE) note: observed one regression case where chunked-prefill increased p99 for low-concurrency customers. Proposed conditional rollout: enable chunked-prefill only when batch_size * seq_length > threshold OR when hot-cache false.
2026-03-11 - Bench update: added mixed-precision stability check (fallback to fp16 for problematic dims). On H100 we saw numerical drift in attention scores at extreme seq lengths; fallback eliminated gradient-like NaN in synthetic tests. Need test coverage for model logits equality tolerance.
2026-03-12 - Design review: UX for canary toggles in Console needed — expose 'prefill mode: chunked|monolithic|auto' and 'kernel strictness: permissive|balanced|safe'. Assigned a follow-up DES ticket for consoles (DES-412).
2026-03-13 - QA: ran customer scenario suite against runtime-1.20 branch with kernel microtiling and mixed-precision fallback. Results: p50 unchanged, p95 improved modestly, p99 regressed in one synthetic edge-case (very uneven batch size distribution). Added heuristic to penalize kernels that increase allocation variance.
2026-03-14 - Next steps: finalize selector heuristics, land PRs for chunked-prefill and fallback, add canary flags and observability (per-kernel allocation breakdown), and schedule a staged rollout starting with internal clusters. Plan to sync with Support on customer guidance.
Links and artifacts: See linked PRs, dashboards, and design notes below.

work_items:
Implement microtiling scorer that penalizes tile shapes with high warp-fragmentation - assigned to Devon
Add mixed-precision runtime check and fast fallback path to v2-like kernel on numeric instability - assigned to Marina
Integrate chunked-prefill into prefill scheduler with threshold gating - assigned to SRE
Add per-kernel allocation metrics and expose in Console for canary monitoring - assigned to Observability
Create canary rollout plan and customer communication draft - assigned to PM
